title: PREFACE
text:
PREFACE

This thesis began a long time ago. The tradition of Savoy College came to have a part in my knowledge of far-away things in my childhood as I garnered it bit by bit from reminiscent talks of my mother, Mrs. Pamela Paxton Boyd, who attended the College—music, primary, preparatory, and collegiate departments—for the fourteen years of its existence. With passing years its particular corner of my memory became a storehouse of pleasant but somewhat unrelated stories of the students, teachers, and customs of the time.

When, therefore, a more mature appreciation of the significance of this pioneer college to Texan education in the '80s suggested the appropriateness of a thesis on its history, the research was naturally motivated by a strong personal interest and sentiment. Through exchange of many letters and later through personal contacts, the unrelated incidents from my memory store began to take on reality; and the isolated facts began to take on meaning and order. The most helpful source of information throughout the year's work on this thesis has been my mother, who has recognized identified faces in pictures; verified and supplemented information as it came to me; aided in tracing through the degrees of kinship, marriage, and personal relationships, the causes, courses, and methods; and in reliving her college days as the work progressed, supplied the enthusiasm necessary for carrying it through. First place in the long list of those to whom I express gratefulness I therefore accord to my mother.

In the same vein of deep gratitude I acknowledge the enthusiastic and friendly help of my mother's schoolmates—ex-students of Savoy College—who have made possible or more possible the detail of this study by their letters and by entertaining me in their homes and libraries. Their help was so fundamental that their names are officially listed
